title: Enhancing graphene/CNT based electrochemical detection using magneto-nanobioprobes
protocol: Prepare Fe3O4 seeds using a modified co-precipitation method.
Optimize parameters such as Au/Fe salt concentration and time kinetics for monodispersity.
Encapsulate Fe3O4 seeds with Au shells to form Au-coated iron oxide particles.
Separate synthesized nanoparticles from solutions using a lab magnet (10 Tesla).
Carry out high resolution transmission electron microscopy \(HR-TEM\) for characterization.
Conduct line mapping and elemental composition studies to confirm the formation of Fe core and Au shell as single Au/Fe nanostructure.
Reconstitute graphite using a modified Hummer’s method.
Cool the reaction mixture in an ice bath.
Use a sonicator at 96% power for 1 hour.
Filtrate the oxidized GO through an anodized aluminum oxide membrane with a nominal pore size of 0.02 μm.
Drop-cast multiwalled CNTs and GO suspension on the working area of SPE to form rGO/CNT nanocomposite.
Reduce the rGO/CNT nanocomposite electrochemically on the SPE.
Dissolve FeCl₃ \(1.28 M) and FeSO₄·7H₂O \(0.64 M) in 1:2 ratios in deoxygenated water under vigorous stirring in nitrogen environment.
Add a solution of 1.5 M NaOH dropwise into the mixture followed by stirring for 40 min.
Collect black precipitate of magnetite using a permanent magnet and wash with deionized water.
Reconstitute the precipitate at a 1:200 dilution in deionized water.
Add sodium citrate \(155 mM) slowly to the boiling solution under constant stirring for 15 min.
Add 10 ml of gold chloride \(10 mM) immediately into the oxidized magnetic solution on a stirring sonicator to encapsulate iron nanoparticles with gold shells.
Collect Au/Fe NPs by magnetic separation followed by washings with deionised water and reconstitute in 0.5 ml water.
Use de-ionised water, pH ~7.0 and resistivity >18 MΩ-cm for nanoparticle synthesis to avoid flocculation.
Maintain the pH of nanoparticles solution at 7.4 by adding 0.1 M K2CO3 before antibody addition.
Add 100 µl of antibody solution (1 mg/ml in PB) to 1 ml Au/Fe solution under mild stirring conditions.
Incubate the solution at 37 °C for 2 h followed by centrifugation at 12,000 rpm for 30 min to remove unconjugated antibodies.
Wash the pellet twice with 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0) containing 3% BSA.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) and store at 4 °C.
Characterize Ab-Au/Fenanobioprobes morphologically by Scanning Transmission Electron Microscope.
Confirm binding of antibodies to nanoparticles by size profiling using dynamic light scattering system.
Demonstrate change in magnetic properties of Au/Fe NPs and their subsequent functionalization with specific antibodies using SQUID analysis.
Vacuum concentrate and completely dry samples for SQUID analysis.
Coat the microtiter ELISA plates with 100 µl of hapten-protein conjugate (10 µg/ml) prepared in carbonate buffer.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C for 2 hours followed by washing with PBST (three times).
Block unbound protein binding sites with 10% defatted skimmed milk (prepared in PBS) for 1 h at 37 °C.
Wash plates with PBST (three times).
Develop competitive inhibition immunoassay format by coating ELISA plates with DCPU–BSA conjugate following the steps given in Box 3.
Synthesize GO by oxidation of exfoliated graphite using modified Hummer’s method from graphite powders using NaNO₃, H₂SO₄, and KMnO₄ in an ice bath.
Filter GO through anodized aluminium oxide membrane with a nominal pore size of 0.02 μm.
Peel off the thin GO film from the AAO filter after air drying.
Mix high aspect ratio pristine multiwalled CNTs and the prepared GO in DMF and water (1:1).
Sonicate the mixture for 1 hour at 96% power.
Drop-cast 5 μl of the suspension on the working area of SPEs.
Incubate the drop-casted SPEs in a vacuum oven for 1 hour at 60 °C.
Apply a potential reductive scan from 0 to -1.5 V with a scan rate of 0.1 V/s for electrochemical conversion of rGO/CNT nanocomposites on SPE.
Characterize the formed nanohybrid by TEM and Raman spectroscopy.
Completely dry the samples in vacuum oven for 1 hour at approximately 60°C.
Scrap off the dried samples from the surface and perform TEM analysis on a carbon coated copper grid (#300 mesh) dropcasted with sample followed by drying in air for 15 minutes.
Mix as prepared Ab-Au/Fe nanobioprobes (1:5 dilution) with varying concentrations of diuron (0.01 pg/ml - 1 μg/ml).
Add 50 µl of the mixture into each well of microtiter plate and incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Place a strong magnet beneath the plate to speed up immunocomplex formation and separate it.
Wash the immunocomplex formed on the plates with PB.
Transfer 50 μl of the solution to the rGO/CNT modified SPE surface.
Apply a reductive scan from 0 to -1.5 V to burst Fe₂O₃ nanoparticles into Fe²⁺ ions.
Observe a characteristic broad reductive peak at -0.75 V.
Use differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) with an amplitude of 50 mV, pulse width of 0.2 s, and pulse period of 0.5 s.
